extracted.intended_audience: immigration applicants, immigration attorneys/practitioners, DHS/USCIS adjudicators, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how DHS/USCIS will assess whether an alien is likely at any time to become a public charge using a totality-of-the-circumstances framework (Form I-944) including specific factors, thresholds, time windows, and evidentiary rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Totality of the circumstances framework / Form I-944
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien’s likelihood of becoming a public charge is prospective and based on the totality of the alien’s circumstances. The Form I-944, Declaration of Self-Sufficiency, would be used by DHS to assess whether the alien is likely to become a public charge based on the totality of the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 33 summarizes the framework: multiple statutory and evidentiary factors (age, health, family status, assets/resources/financial status, receipt of public benefits, education/skills, etc.) are considered together; DHS assigns weights (e.g., heavily weighed positive/negative) to individual factors and makes a forward-looking determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether alien's age affects ability to work: 18 ≤ age ≤ 61; age > 61; age < 18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight: The degree to which age makes the alien more or less likely to become a public charge by impacting ability to work. Examples: Positive finding — 18 ≤ age ≤ 61. Negative findings — Age > 61 unless alien can demonstrate employment or sufficient household assets and resources; Age < 18 unless alien can demonstrate employment or sufficient household assets and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of any medical condition(s) that (1) is likely to require extensive treatment or institutionalization, or (2) will interfere with the alien's ability to care for him- or herself, to attend school, or to work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight: The degree to which health makes the alien more or less likely to become a public charge. Positive: Absence of such conditions. Negative: Presence of such conditions. (Used to determine ability to provide/care for self, attend school, or work.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Family status / household composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether alien has a household that he or she supports; whether another household is supporting the alien; alien’s household size in relation to household assets and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight: Family status can be positive or negative. Consider household size relative to assets/resources (e.g., among noncitizens in families of 3 or 4 about 20% received non-cash assistance vs ~30% for families of 5+).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assets, resources, and financial status — considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider annual gross household income (excluding public benefits); additional income from individuals not included in household who physically reside with the alien; additional ongoing income from outside the household; household cash assets and resources (checking/savings for 12 months); non-cash assets convertible to cash within 12 months (net cash value of real estate, annuities, securities, retirement/education accounts, etc.); financial liabilities; credit history and credit score; private health insurance or financial resources for medical expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighting guidance: Heavily Weighed Positive — household assets, resources, and support ≥ 250% of the FPG for the household size; alien is authorized to work and currently employed with annual household income ≥ 250% of the FPG. Heavily Weighed Negative — alien cannot demonstrate current employment, employment history, or reasonable prospect of future employment; alien is currently receiving one or more public benefits (as defined in 8 CFR 212.21(b)); alien has received one or more public benefits (see additional entries). Evidence sources: checking/savings statements covering 12 months prior to filing, documentation of income, asset documentation, credit reports, insurance records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income thresholds: 250% of FPG and 125–250% of FPG
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS proposes to consider it a heavily weighed positive factor if the alien has financial assets, resources, support, or annual income of at least 250 percent of the FPG in the totality of the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Income between 125 and 250 percent of the FPL is considered a positive factor in the public charge inadmissibility analysis. However, an alien with annual income less than 250% of FPG would not automatically be inadmissible; all factors are considered in the totality of the circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt, certification, or approval to receive public benefits (post-effective-date) — 15% threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits received on or after the effective date are considered if the aggregate annual value of benefits received since the effective date exceeds 15 percent of the FPG for the household size within any consecutive 12-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the aggregate annual value exceeds the 15% FPG threshold for the relevant household size and period, DHS will consider the receipt; certification to receive such benefits in an amount exceeding the threshold is a heavily weighed negative factor in the totality of the circumstances (even if actual received to date is lower). Example: For household of 1 with FPG $12,140, 15% = $1,821; certified receipt of $2,160 would be heavily weighed negative. Receipt within 36 months of application can be heavily weighed negative per proposed 8 CFR 212.22(c)(1)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of benefits received before effective date (previously excluded/included benefits)
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS would not consider public benefits under proposed 8 CFR 212.21(b) that were previously excluded under the 1999 Interim Field Guidance if received before effective date of the final rule, except benefits previously considered under the 1999 Interim Field Guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits excluded under the 1999 Interim Field Guidance and received before the effective date would not be considered. Benefits that were considered under the 1999 Interim Field Guidance (e.g., cash assistance for income maintenance including SSI, TANF, GA, and benefits for long-term institutionalization) received prior to the effective date would be considered as a negative factor in the totality of the circumstances but would not be considered a 'heavily weighed negative factor.' Table 29 summarizes consideration before/after effective date. DHS seeks comment on whether to consider such past benefits at all or to treat them differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportional valuation and calculation of benefits (SNAP / EBT example)
rubrics_metrics.description: For SNAP benefits, DHS would calculate the value of the benefit attributable to the alien in proportion to the total number of people covered by the benefit, based on the amounts deposited in the Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A household of three receives $2,400 SNAP in a 12-month period; proportional share attributable to the alien = $800 (one-third). For purposes of the 15% threshold, DHS sums proportional amounts attributable to the alien across monetizable benefits during the relevant consecutive 12-month period. Certified future amounts are counted toward the certified total for the consecutive 12-month period even if not yet disbursed as of adjudication; termination letters and other evidence will be weighed in the totality of the circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification / evidence of future receipt and mitigators (termination letters, evidence of stopped receipt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification to receive public benefits (or approval to receive) on or after the effective date may make those benefits count toward the 15% threshold and be heavily weighed negative; conversely, evidence such as a benefits termination letter can be weighed to show unlikelihood of future receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in Tables 30–32 show: (1) Certification for future benefits that exceeds 15% FPG is heavily weighed negative even if amounts actually received as of adjudication are below threshold; (2) A termination letter suggesting future benefits have stopped is weighed along with other evidence and may mitigate the negative weight. DHS will consider timing (received within 36 months), certification duration (e.g., 36 months), and whether receipt is ongoing or terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment history and reasonable prospect of future employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the alien can demonstrate current employment, employment history, or a reasonable prospect of future employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heavily Weighed Negative: Alien cannot demonstrate current employment, employment history, or reasonable prospect of future employment. Heavily Weighed Positive (related): alien authorized to work and currently employed with annual household income ≥ 250% FPG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of past cash income-maintenance benefits and institutionalization under 1999 Field Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the 1999 Interim Field Guidance the current or past receipt of cash benefits for income maintenance or long-term institutionalization at government expense should be taken into account under the totality of the circumstances test; past receipt does not automatically make an alien inadmissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The longer ago an alien received such cash benefits or was institutionalized, the less weight those factors will have; the length of time and amount received are relevant — longer receipt and greater amounts imply a stronger likelihood of becoming a public charge. Past receipt may be overcome by positive factors demonstrating ability to be self-supporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other discrete evidentiary factors listed under Assets/Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Applied for or received any public benefit as defined in 8 CFR 212.21(b) on or after the effective date; been certified or approved to receive public benefits on or after the effective date; applied for or received a fee waiver for an immigration benefit request on or after the effective date; credit history and credit score; private health insurance or financial resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are specific considerations under the 'Assets, Resources, and Financial Status' factor and will be evaluated for their positive or negative implications in the totality of the circumstances. For example, applying for/receiving a fee waiver on or after the effective date is a factor to be considered; credit history may indicate ability to support oneself; lack of insurance may be negative if health risk exists.
